title: Technology Risk Management - Lead Associate
description: Playing an essential role in the U.S. economy, Fannie Mae is foundational to housing finance. Here, your expertise can help fuel purpose-driven innovation that expands access to homeownership and affordable rental housing across the country. Join Fannie Mae to grow your career and help people find a place to call home. Job Description As a valued colleague on our team, you will provide risk guidance and support assessments that identify and evaluate technology operational risks that could affect our reputation, resilience, security, regulatory obligations, and financial performance. You will collaborate with key stakeholders across the enterprise to understand business and technology objectives, provide effective challenge, and support risk-informed decisions across RCSA, technology assessments, issue management, event management, artificial intelligence, and data analytics. THE IMPACT YOU WILL MAKE The Technology Risk Management - Lead Associate role will offer you the flexibility to make each day your own, while working alongside people who care so that you can deliver on the following responsibilities: Key responsibilities include: Serve as a Technology Operational Risk Lead, providing risk guidance and advise stakeholders across technology processes, systems, and change initiatives. Support Risk and Control Self-Assessment (RCSA) activities, including risk identification, control evaluation, evidence review, issue escalation, and residual risk analysis. Conduct technology risk assessments and synthesize findings into clear, decision-ready analyses and reports for business and risk stakeholders. Support issue management throughout the lifecycle, including root-cause evaluation, remediation planning, milestone monitoring, evidence review, and closure validation. Support operational risk event management by assessing events, analyzing impacts and trends, documenting lessons learned, and monitoring corrective actions. Evaluate risks associated with artificial intelligence and emerging technologies, including responsible use, data, model, security, resilience, and governance considerations. Use data analytics and visualization techniques to identify risk trends, improve monitoring, and communicate actionable insights to stakeholders. THE EXPERIENCE YOU BRING TO THE TEAM Minimum Required Experiences 4 years of experience in technology risk, operational risk, information technology audit, cybersecurity risk, compliance, or a related field. Working knowledge of RCSA, technology risk assessments, issue management, and operational risk event management practices. Strong interpersonal, collaboration, and influencing skills, with the ability to build effective relationships across technology, business, risk, audit, and compliance teams. Ability to communicate complex risk concepts clearly in written reports, presentations, and discussions with technical and nontechnical stakeholders. Knowledge of artificial intelligence concepts, associated technology and operational risks, and responsible AI governance practices. Proficiency in data analysis, including the ability to interpret datasets, identify trends, and develop actionable risk insights using common analytics and visualization tools. Shows curiosity and adaptability in learning and responsibly applying new technologies, including artificial intelligence, to reimagine how we work. Desired Experiences 5–10 years of experience in technology risk, operational risk, information technology audit, cybersecurity risk, compliance, or a related field. Bachelor's degree or equivalent relevant experience. Experience in financial services or another highly regulated industry. Experience with governance, risk, and compliance platforms and data visualization tools such as Power BI or Tableau. Familiarity with technology and cybersecurity frameworks such as NIST, COBIT, or similar industry standards. Relevant certification such as CRISC, CISA, CISSP, or an equivalent risk, audit, or technology credential. #LI-Hybrid Qualifications Education: Bachelor's Level Degree (Required) The future is what you make it to be. title: Lead Governance, Risk and Compliance Manager
description: Opportunity Overview We’re looking for an experienced Lead Governance, Risk and Compliance (GRC) Manager to lead and mature our enterprise security governance, risk management, regulatory compliance, and customer assurance programs. In this role, you will drive operational excellence across compliance frameworks, security risk management, third-party assurance, and customer-facing security initiatives while strengthening the processes and technology that support our growing business. This is a hands-on leadership role suited for an experienced GRC professional who can independently manage complex initiatives, influence cross-functional stakeholders, and build scalable, repeatable operations. You’ll work closely with Security, Engineering, IT, Legal, Sales, Customer Success, and executive leadership to advance our security posture, accelerate customer trust, and enable business growth. What you’ll do: Lead and mature Cohere’s GRC program, establishing scalable governance processes, operating procedures, risk management practices, and measurable performance indicators aligned with business objectives. Own the deployment, configuration, and optimization of enterprise GRC platforms, including control mapping, evidence automation, risk registers, continuous monitoring, and compliance reporting. Direct compliance and certification initiatives across HITRUST, HIPAA, ISO 27001, and applicable regulatory requirements, ensuring ongoing audit readiness and effective control execution. Lead customer security assurance activities, including security questionnaires, due diligence requests, customer audits, executive briefings, and security discussions with prospective and existing clients. Partner with Sales, Customer Success, and Marketing to develop security-focused go-to-market materials, establish and maintain a customer-facing Trust Center, and strengthen security as a competitive differentiator. Review and negotiate security-related contractual requirements in partnership with Legal, including Data Protection Agreements (DPAs), Business Associate Agreements (BAAs), security exhibits, and customer security obligations. Oversee enterprise risk management activities, including risk assessments, remediation tracking, exception management, and the enforcement and reporting of vulnerability remediation SLAs across Engineering, Platform, DevOps, and Data teams. Govern identity and access compliance, including periodic access reviews, privileged access certifications, segregation of duties, and remediation of access control deficiencies. Establish and maintain cross-functional GRC engagement with business units to align security policies, controls, risk ownership, and compliance obligations with operational priorities. Develop and deliver executive-level presentations, dashboards, and reporting that communicate compliance posture, risk exposure, remediation performance, customer assurance metrics, and program maturity. Build and scale a high-performing GRC function, establishing repeatable processes, developing team capabilities, managing external assessors and partners, and driving continuous improvement with minimal day-to-day oversight. What you’ll need: 8+ years of progressive experience in information security, governance, risk management, compliance, or IT audit, including 2+ years leading GRC initiatives, programs, and/or teams. Professional certifications such as CISM, CISSP, CRISC, CISA, CGRC, or HITRUST CCSFP. Deep working knowledge of HITRUST, ISO 27001, and HIPAA including direct experience managing assessments, implementing controls, coordinating audits, and maintaining certification readiness. Demonstrated experience deploying and administering enterprise GRC platforms, including implementation, workflow design, control mapping, evidence collection, reporting, and process automation. Familiarity with the NIST Cybersecurity Framework, NIST AI Risk Management Framework, ISO 27017, ISO 27018, ISO 42001, and privacy-related security requirements. Deep understanding of enterprise risk management, including risk registers, control assessments, risk treatment plans, vulnerability remediation SLAs, and formal exception management. Demonstrated project and program management capabilities, including managing concurrent initiatives, developing operational roadmaps, establishing KPIs, and delivering results independently. Proven experience leading customer assurance programs, including security questionnaires, customer-facing security meetings, due diligence reviews, and responding to enterprise customer requirements. Experience with GRC platforms such as Vanta, Anecdotes, ZenGRC, Drata, ServiceNow GRC, or similar enterprise solutions. Demonstrated success developing GRC program maturity models, executive scorecards, and risk-based reporting frameworks. title: Associate Director, Information Governance and Records Management
description: About the Role: Grade Level (for internal use): 12 The Team: The Data Privacy, Protection and Governance team at S&P Global is dedicated to managing sensitive, personal, and non-personal information. We achieve this through the implementation of comprehensive policies, processes, controls, and metrics that ensure compliance with global regulations. The Impact: S&P Global is seeking an Director, Information Governance and Records Management to lead, mature, and scale the enterprise-wide information governance and records management program across its global data and analytics business, with supporting responsibility for data governance, privacy by design, and AI governance. This role owns the strategy, policies, standards, and controls that govern the full lifecycle of S&P Global’s business records and information, from creation and capture through classification, retention, legal hold, and defensible disposition. The Director will ensure that records and information management practices align with S&P Global’s Information Governance Policy framework, Privacy Program, and evolving legal, regulatory, and recordkeeping obligations across jurisdictions. The position plays a critical leadership role in operationalizing the enterprise records retention schedule, strengthening information classification compliance, and reducing over-retention risk, while supporting a risk-based data management and governance model, privacy by design, and responsible AI practices that underpin S&P Global’s delivery of data-driven products and services, including analytics, ratings, market intelligence, and entity-based data solutions. S&P Global’s business model—focused on delivering data, analytics, and insight to global markets—requires robust governance over data sourcing, processing, retention, and usage to ensure trust, regulatory compliance, and operational resilience. What’s in it for you: In this role, you will: Collaborate with senior and executive stakeholders globally. Act as a senior advisor to stakeholders across Legal, Compliance, Technology, and business divisions. Lead cross-functional governance forums to drive alignment and accountability for data governance activities. Be an integral part of building and maturing the global Information Governance and Records Management program, working alongside executive leadership to drive our team forward. Responsibilities: The Associate Director, Information Governance and Records Management will be responsible for: Information Governance & Records Management Leadership Lead the strategy, design, implementation, and continuous improvement of the enterprise Information Governance and Records Management program, covering the full information lifecycle (creation, capture, use, storage, retention, legal hold, and defensible disposition) across paper and electronic records. Own and maintain core policies and standards, including: Information Governance Policy Information Classification Standard Records Retention Schedule Legal Hold and Defensible Disposition procedures Ensure alignment with regulatory requirements, internal risk frameworks, and international standards. Maintain and periodically refresh the global Records Retention Schedule, conducting legal and regulatory retention research across jurisdictions and securing business sign-off on record classes and retention periods. Drive operational adoption of retention requirements across business divisions and enterprise systems, including records inventories, system-level retention configuration, and coordinated defensible disposition of records and data that have met their retention periods. Partner with Legal and eDiscovery teams to manage the legal hold process and ensure holds override routine disposition. Develop and deliver information governance and records management training, communications, and a network of divisional records coordinators. Data Classification & Information Handling Establish and oversee enterprise-wide data classification frameworks and compliance monitoring. Partner with Information Security and technology teams to ensure appropriate controls for data access, storage, and protection. Implement and track metrics to measure classification compliance and data handling effectiveness. Data Management & Governance Support the development of a scalable, enterprise data management and governance model that integrates with records and retention requirements, including: Data inventory and cataloging Data ownership and stewardship Data flow visibility and control Collaborate with business, technology, and risk teams to ensure governance controls are embedded across products, platforms, and operations. Risk Management & Regulatory Readiness Identify, assess, and mitigate risks relating to data governance, retention, classification, and regulatory compliance. title: AI Tech Risk Officer
description: This is Adyen Adyen provides payments, data, and financial products in a single solution for customers like Meta, Uber, H&M, and Microsoft - making us the financial technology platform of choice. At Adyen, everything we do is engineered for ambition.  For our teams, we create an environment with opportunities for our people to succeed, backed by the culture and support to ensure they are enabled to truly own their careers. We are motivated individuals who tackle unique technical challenges at scale and solve them as a team. Together, we deliver innovative and ethical solutions that help businesses achieve their ambitions faster. AI Tech Risk Officer  Adyen combines the agility of a global tech company with the stability of a licensed financial institution. As a Tech Risk Officer focused on AI technology, you will partner with cross-functional teams and regional second-line functions (such as Model risk, Compliance and the DPO office) to ensure safe, secure, and resilient implementation of autonomous AI architectures and regulatory requirements. The Tech Risk team, part of the second line risk function ensures that risk management practices are applied across Adyen’s technological environments, teams and initiatives. This continuous task requires a close and supporting relationship with tech teams in the first line, in order to understand changes in the tech landscape but also to guide them in relation to risk mitigations.  In this role, you will focus on the unique security and architectural risks associated with building, deploying, and monitoring autonomous AI agents, working closely with first-line engineering teams to embed risk mitigation into technical design. You will be part of building technology, challenging design and execution through constructive and positive conversations. Realize better outcomes together.  The ideal candidate is a risk or tech professional with hands-on experience evaluating and managing risks arising from the implementation of AI solutions, software architecture for agentic systems and the underlying tech stack. You have a technical background that enables you to evaluate agentic workflows, models safety, and integration points, advancing our second-line risk framework to support safe AI innovation at scale. Both security as well as IT-resilience experience is welcome.  What you will do  Evaluate technology threats and risks  across diverse AI developments in the industry, internal projects and assets, advising stakeholders and ensuring risk mitigation actions are implemented.  Collaborate closely with leadership and build an internal network to ensure the domain remains represented in business activities, contributing to decision making.  Drive the second line risk oversight for AI and general Technology risks, including KRI design, risk monitoring and reporting.  Collaborate with other Risk domains, in order to incorporate AI Tech risks into Adyen’s risk profile, ensuring those are considered when evaluating company objectives.  Collaborate with or advise other second-line teams (typically Regulatory, Compliance and Privacy) in the implementation of AI Governance requirements in Adyen’s tech environments, as well as engage with local auditors or external partners (externally) as a trusted point of contact for the specific risk domain, globally.  Engage with various regulators to provide clarity on Adyen’s IT Resilience and excellence landscape. Who you are You have at least 5+ years experience within a risk management function, with 2 years of demonstrated experience guiding AI risk mitigations, AI Governance or AI Cyber Security.   Demonstrated experience evaluating technology risks, Security best practices and associated industry and regulatory frameworks.  You feel comfortable explaining risks associated with IT environments to engineers but also to business stakeholders.  You have a solid understanding of commonly used AI technology stack (hardware, software, network and systems, on-prem or cloud solutions), at the level required to identify risks or weaknesses and recommend tangible actions, design metrics to enable risk monitoring and oversight.  You are innovative, flexible with strong problem-solving capabilities and able to define effective processes, when possible scaling manual processes via automation.  Available to work from our New York or San Francisco office and travel to other offices periodically. Fluent in English, both written and spoken. Any additional language is a plus.   Compensation The base salary range for this role is $145,000- $260,000. title: Principal Security Engineer, AI Governance
description: What You Can Expect As a Senior Security Engineer on Zoom's Enterprise Security team, you will own the AI Governance program end to end, defining the technical standards and risk posture that determine how Zoom adopts AI safely and at scale. On any given day, you will be assessing emerging AI use cases, building security frameworks for GenAI and agentic systems, and serving as the trusted technical voice on AI security for engineering and enterprise stakeholders across four critical domains. This is a hands-on, highly autonomous role that calls for real depth in both AI/ML systems and security engineering; candidates without working familiarity with how modern AI introduces security risk will not be set up for success here. You will work as part of a globally distributed, multi-domain security engineering team, collaborating closely with colleagues across time zones and contributing across adjacent security domains beyond AI. About the Team Zoom's Enterprise Security team is the engineering foundation behind how the company identifies, contains, and gets ahead of risk across its most critical systems. Working across AI, data, network, endpoint, and cloud security, the team builds the controls, standards, and architectures that let Zoom move quickly without creating unacceptable exposure. As Zoom deepens its investment in AI across Zoom Workplace and its broader platform, this team's work is increasingly central to how the company grows responsibly. Responsibilities Own the AI governance risk register and end-to-end assessment methodology across four domains (GenAI, Agentic AI, Shadow AI/Local AI, and AI Gateway/MCP); conduct and review risk evaluations using Likelihood x Impact scoring and drive remediation with owning engineering teams. Identify and prioritize security gaps in GenAI deployments including prompt injection, data leakage, model misuse, and insecure output handling; define monitoring and guardrail requirements for agentic systems operating with significant autonomy and tool access. Lead the Shadow AI governance strategy end to end, from quantifying risk exposure to recommending and operationalizing detection and enforcement controls across the enterprise. Set the security bar for AI gateway and Model Context Protocol (MCP) implementations, including secure configuration, access control frameworks, and governance coverage. Architect reference security patterns for AI adoption (AI gateways, MCP servers, agent frameworks, LLM integrations) and serve as design authority in AI-related architecture reviews; translate the AI Governance Risk Charter into a concrete roadmap of technical requirements and measurable outcomes. Drive evaluations of AI security tooling (AI gateways, CASB/SWG, agentic monitoring, MCP governance solutions), including POC design, cost-benefit analysis, and leadership recommendations; author and maintain security standards and policy for AI adoption. Lead security architecture reviews and risk assessments across adjacent domains including Network, Endpoint, Cloud, and Data Security; contribute to incident response, detection engineering, and purple team exercises as shared team functions. Serve as the primary technical partner to AI/ML, engineering, and enterprise teams; lead cross-functional working groups, mentor engineers on risk analysis and documentation quality, and deliver clear reporting on AI risk posture and forecasted challenges to leadership. What We're Looking For 10+ years of security engineering or cybersecurity experience, including end-to-end ownership of a security domain or program, with a track record of driving risk assessment, prioritization, and remediation across cross-functional teams. Solid working knowledge of modern AI/ML systems and the security risks they introduce (LLMs, generative AI, agentic systems); direct experience securing GenAI or LLM-based applications in an enterprise environment is a strong differentiator. Understanding of AI gateways, Model Context Protocol (MCP), CASB/SWG, or DLP tooling, and a working understanding of shadow AI detection and governance strategies. Working knowledge across core security domains (network, endpoint, cloud, and data security) sufficient to independently lead architecture reviews and risk assessments outside of AI. Experience designing security reference architectures or serving as a design authority in complex, cross-functional technical environments; threat modeling experience applied to AI or novel technology stacks is a plus. Demonstrated ability to influence senior stakeholders, communicate risk clearly in writing and verbally, and drive alignment across engineering, product, and enterprise teams without direct authority. Comfort operating in a globally distributed team with regular overlap with US Pacific hours; ability to work with high autonomy and produce clear, actionable risk documentation for leadership audiences.
